title: Siegard materialized knowledge graph
description: Contract for knowledge/graph.json, the materialized form of a knowledge base. The ontology defers this schema to the materializer, and this distribution ships none. The artifact is derived and R42 forbids hand-editing it. It exists because expansion, impact analysis, and the projections all need the same resolved graph, and a versioned schema is required for data a downstream agent parses to reach a decision. `edge_kinds` makes the graph self-describing: a consumer reads the traversal policy R19 requires from the artifact rather than from whatever materialized it. A node carries no status: `knowledge-graph/1` mirrored the knowledge object's, and ADR-0018 removed both, so every node in the graph is a current fact and expansion has nothing to filter on.

contract_version.description: A consumer rejects an artifact it was not built to read rather than inferring version from shape.

edge_kinds.description: The closed edge vocabulary of spec 0003 R17, with the cardinality R18 requires enforced and the traversal policy R19 requires declared. Keyed by edge name.

origin_types.description: Node types that may declare this edge. Absent or empty means any knowledge object.

target_types.description: Node types this edge may name. Absent or empty means any node.

inverse_maximum.description: How many edges of this kind may arrive at one target. This is how R20's at-most-one-lifecycle-per-definition becomes a check.

traversed.description: Whether expansion follows this edge. R19 requires the policy to be declared, and expansion MUST follow only traversed edges.

crosses_context.description: Whether this edge is exempt from R15. True only for the three edges whose purpose is to leave or to name a partition.

nodes.description: Every permanent node, ordered lexicographically by id so identical input produces byte-identical output.

kind.description: The six knowledge-object types, plus `adr`. An ADR is a node and never a knowledge object (R7).

question.description: The retrieval key. Absent on an ADR, which answers why rather than what.

context.description: The bounded context the boundary chain resolves to. Absent on an ADR and on a bounded context itself.

edges.description: Every declared relationship. Only a declared relationship is an edge: a relationship inferred from prose is not, because two readings of one paragraph produce two graphs.

locator.description: Where in the source's frontmatter this edge was declared, so a report names the field rather than the file.
